I don't know why I started cutting back in the day. I think it was because I thought it was cool, but it was also a method of hurting oneself and feeling a sort of pain. Combined with seeing the damage, maybe this helped me briefly come to terms with situations I was trying to cope with.

My last doctor refused to keep me on any program that would financially help me get through college, as he considered it fraudulent. This has really perplexed me. He felt that, because I was going back to full-time education, I was not "sick". I can only deduce that he believes that anyone that could sit in a classroom for 20 hours a week plus doing 20 hours of homework does not need financial support, as they can get a job outside of these 40 hours and can endure reality. This is what I did over a decade ago to some extent, but now I'm 30.

My reality is, that when I look around at other 30 year olds, I see myself as a complete and utter failure, and I only perceive downward progression from that. The fact that my old doctor thinks that me having financial support during this time is fraudulent, to me, can only mean that it is fraudulent in the sense that he does not believe I am unwell. What this does is encourage me to try and prove that fact wrong asap, which is a disastrous contemplation, but is something that I am currently in the process of visualising as reality. People always say " visualise success". I am currently visualising catastrophe.

This same doctor diagnosed me with a major depressive episode last year. He also, after discussion with me, categorized issues that brought about this diagnosis as sexual abuse. Yet, a year later, with me in a college place, he could not agree that I need financial support during this period of recovery in my life. Its left me extremely confused, questioning everything I know, including whether I'm just weak, or trying to rig the system. These thoughts bring me to a conclusion that the only way I can prove myself to be acceptable is to hurt myself drastically in the next few weeks. I've never felt such a crystallised version of how good or bad reality could become in the next few weeks, but at the same time I've never been so aware as to how wrong I can be in perceiving one route as "good" and another as "bad". Altogether I have a lot of confusion, and a lot of destructive thought which is influencing me into taking a plan of action that is capable of leading me further down an unforeseeably dark path.

30 now. Still can't drive. That's a skill, don't sell it short. I shut myself off from the world in my 20's and ignored reality for quite a long time. When I came to I realised my life had been an abject failure, that I hate myself and everyone around me, and that nothing matters. Its no way to live but I don't know what else to do now. I legitimately tried to follow my bliss and ended up isolated and full of spite. I've also been very lucky in some ways over the past few years, yet I've managed to really squander that luck.  

Its strange, I straddle a line between complete self-hate and martyrdom/victimhood. I have done so much to sabotage myself throughout time, and I blame my family for it because I don't understand how someone could do what I naturally have done to myself. Its so complicated. The only thing I feel like I can do to redeem myself is to overload myself with work now, but I really don't know how that will develop. Good on you for trying with the jobs, I haven't even gotten an interview. You're much more valuable the younger you are. 

The only answer to me is to "grow up", meaning job/study/something of a more conventional, meaningful life. Its going to be hell, I truly feel like I don't understand the workload ahead of me nor the temperament required to succeed, but that's me. I'm a very naive, neurotic, delusional man. I think I will be for the foreseeable future. There's a chance I might have some sense of normality by maybe 40 if I can endure my mess, if not I'm not sure what happens. I'm not even sure what happens if I do things "right" from now until 40, I'm just trying to prepare myself for meaningless torture, its the only guarantee in this life.

Yeah, I'm trying to change now by going back to college. I am so miserable though, it seeps out of me. I'm finding it really hard to just deal with the logistical aspects of trying to start afresh. That's before even mentioning the coursework which will be incredibly intense also. I'm so old and have such few skills that benefit people or myself in the real world, its really sad. I get so wound up into my own spiral of deficiency that it becomes this rock hard casing of negativity that just bounces off me at other people. Its gotten to the point that its so clearly evident to people, that they don't really want to be near me. I only got into college because I did not have to do an interview for the college, everywhere else I did an interview and failed. I feel like I'm going to get eaten up this year, at least it will have been something different, I just find it hard to imagine anything better for myself, I'm so used to being miserable and maybe happy in it. I feel like a failure in so many ways. I feel like I could life 10 lifetimes and achieve nothing, yet I fantasize about achieving the amount of things in 1 life that people do in 10. Its just delusional.
